**Review Rating**: 5.0
- Quality: 5.0

**The Reviewer**
Digital Marketing Director for Education Management Centers
- Industry: Education


- Review Type: Phone Interview
- Verified

**The Review** — May 5, 2021

**Feedback Summary**: Flexible and caring, Ignite Visibility has proven themselves to be a committed partner. From significant traffic improvement to an increased number of qualified leads, they've also succeeded in terms of metrics. Ignite Visbility also offers knowledge sharing and transparency into project management. 
""Ignite answers a question, tells us why it is important, and makes sure that we understand their response." 
"

**BACKGROUND**
Introduce your business and what you do there.

I am the director of digital marketing for a franchise with 90 plus centers across the country. We offer in-center and online programs for children and adults who wish to improve their brain’s physical performance. Our customers range from people with ADHD, Dyslexia, or learning challenges or disorders, all the way to folks who simply want to up their game a bit. We work with kids aged 4–18, and we also have adult programs.

**OPPORTUNITY / CHALLENGE**
What challenge were you trying to address with Ignite Visibility?

I brought them in initially to help with our SEO by fully migrating our site onto HubSpot, as part of it was still on WordPress.

**SOLUTION**
What was the scope of their involvement? 

Originally, we were going to migrate and redesign our site all at once, but we made a business decision to break it apart so that we could better track performance internally. Right now, they are redesigning our entire website.

Our website now is very old and outdated — it doesn’t represent our brand or communicate well to our users. It utilizes a lot of text and doesn’t have a very good UX. We wanted to bring it up to date with the new brand standards we’d been working on, as well as create a better that’s easier to understand, scan, and read, and ultimately convert with. Another company is helping with our brand refresh and messaging, and we communicate their work to Ignite for the latter to implement in the design.

We also have a monthly SEO retainer with them.

What is the team composition?

We have Jason (Senior SEO Strategist) and Oscar (VP of Creative) on the SEO side, as well as two other people on the development team. Ignite Visibility also uses offshore developers. I’ve also worked with the head developer, and she is awesome.

We got to a place where we had done a couple of revisions, but the design wasn’t exactly where we needed it to be. We were working with a junior designer on the team, so we asked Oscar (VP of Creative) to bring on a more senior resource to get us across the finish line. He was absolutely supportive and willing to do that.

How did you come to work with Ignite Visibility?

I worked with Ignite at a previous company for about two years. One of my colleagues there had done some research, and we liked the client base that they had, and John (Co-Founder and CEO) was rated 2017 Search Engine Expert of the Year.

We also liked how straightforward and clearly they communicated, and their strategies sounded logical. We were doing a CMS migration similar to one they’d done for another of their customers, and they accomplished that without causing a dip in traffic. We were really interested in that piece.

Here at my current job, my boss brought on Ignite Visibility before I joined the team. She’d worked with them at her previous post, which, coincidentally, was also at my old company. I came to my current post during the RFP process and viewed everyone’s materials. I chose Ignite after a series of final interviews.

How much have you invested in them?

We have invested around $25,000–$50,000 with them so far.

What is the status of this engagement?

We signed the statement of work in October 2020. The project is ongoing; once they finalize the design with signoff from all our stakeholders, they’ll launch the site. We don’t have a hard date yet, as we’re waiting for the design to get where it needs to be.

**RESULTS & FEEDBACK**
What evidence can you share that demonstrates the impact of the engagement?

I don’t know what the design output is going to be, but I have seen the senior designer’s previous work, and I am very excited about it. 

From February–March, we saw pretty great gains in our SEO performance, including a lift in the number of keywords that our blog had on page one. In March only, we gained 132 keywords. Our franchise ventures each have their own page, and, collectively, those pages saw a lift month over month. They grew by 20% in sessions and 21% in users. Organic traffic to the homepage was up 10%.

Ignite Visibility had an insight that 21 of our top 22 top-visited pages were blog posts, and they recommended that we add an inquiry form to our blog post. We did that, and we are seeing inquiries come through from it.

There have been a couple of bumps along the road, but there have only been a few migrations in my career that have gone perfectly. When a couple of things happened, Ignite Visibility’s team handled them very well, working hard without complaining. They treated the migration just like I would have, and I am responsible for owning it. I felt like we were all a part of the exact same team.

How did Ignite Visibility perform from a project management standpoint?

It started off a little rocky. I came to meetings with questions that I expected the team to answer, and I communicated my expectations when that didn’t happen. Ignite Visibility listened to us and was able to change, pick up the pace, and come more prepared. I have been very happy with that ever since that communication.

We started out with two separate weekly Zoom calls: one for the SEO team and one with the web development team to discuss feedback. Ignite recommended that we form a single call so that everyone can hear each other. We talk about SEO first and design and develop second, and it’s been very beneficial for both our team and Ignite. I also send them emails if I think of other questions between our meetings.

We set the agenda for the meetings the day ahead of time. Ignite sends me a notice of what the agenda is, and then I add my questions and topics that I want to cover so that they can prepare.

What did you find most impressive about them?

It’s been clear that Ignite Visibility cares about its customers since I first interviewed them at my previous job. Additionally, their strategy revolves around performance, and not just for organic traffic, but sales. I don’t care if I see a 20% lift in organic traffic if it’s not bringing me qualified traffic and increasing leads. They are very accommodating in our standing in that aspect.

I also like how transparent they are about sharing case studies, as well as the templates that they use to track projects. This shows us how detailed they are and what their process is like. By answering our basic questions, we learned how much pride they take in educating their clients. Other vendors that we’ve worked with respond to our questions with vague, unimpressive answers. Ignite answers a question, tells us why it is important, and makes sure that we understand their response.

Ignite supported us the entire way, diving in without question and successfully completing the migration. I am a part of a very small but mighty team, and I was prepared to do a lot of the heavy lifting myself or bring in interns to get it done. Every time I pose a question to Ignite, like how to perform QA, record all the URLs we’re bringing over, or ensuring our redirects are set up correctly, they explained how they would do it themselves. They alleviated a lot from my plate so that I could work on other tasks.

Finally, we asked them to have a couple of development resources certified in HubSpot, and they were happy to get their people certified.

Are there any areas they could improve?

There are two items I could say. The first is the previously mentioned communication issues, where their team didn’t have answers for questions related to our timeline and tasks that they were owners of. After I communicated that to them, the situation was fixed immediately.

The other issue was the junior designer working on the website. I know that Oscar was working with him to ensure that the deliverable would work for us, but early on we noticed that we weren’t going to get across the finish line with that designer. His deliverables along the way weren’t meeting our expectations, and we gave feedback. They’ve been flexible, thankful, and able to accommodate us. 

Do you have any advice for potential customers?

Ignite can give you advice and insights all day long, but if your company doesn’t take those insights and publish those changes on the website, then nothing will happen. I know this, but putting it into practice is the hardest thing to do. You have to make the recommended changes continuously because it is a 50/50 partnership.

Right now, we’re 2–3 months into the SEO monthly retainer. I have 500 pages of content that I can start updating, but I need approval internally, and that takes time. If you’re in this situation, ask Ignite Visibility what else you can do in the downtime.

### Technical SEO Audit Increased Indexed Pages +130%
Overview:
Our ecommerce client hosts a site with a consistently growing inventory, however, their site wasn’t being indexed properly by Google. By April 2024, 80% of category pages were missing from search results. A small technical fix led to a 130% increase in indexed pages in four months. 
Challenge: 
Our client’s site had over 700,000 pages and relied on multiple XML sitemaps, each of which were maxed out at 50,000 URLs, Google’s limit. Large sitemaps can overwhelm search engines, and without proper indexing, our client’s expansive inventory was practically invisible.
Strategy/Tactics:
We split large XML sitemaps into smaller files of 25,000 URLs and submitted them individually to Google Search Console and Bing. High-value pages were prioritized in the sitemap structure to ensure faster indexing.
Results:
In one week, indexed pages jumped from 99K on April 26 to 110K by May 3. By June 28, the count surged to 154K, reaching 225K by September 20—a 130% increase in four months. This boosted visibility in Google’s ecommerce filters and drove more qualified traffic.

## About the Team

### Our Story
Our vision: beyond visibility is where real growth happens. Founded in San Diego in 2013 by John Lincoln and Krishnan Coughran, Ignite Visibility is now 600+ experts, our Igniters, on one mission: turn digital marketing into a coordinated revenue engine for multi-location, franchise and enterprise brands, Powered by Rallio AI. ### Commonly Asked Questions

**Who will work on my account?**
Your account is staffed from Ignite Visibility's 600+ in-house marketing experts, our Igniters, and led by a senior strategist who owns your results. Depending on your goals, your team draws in specialists across SEO, paid media, social, creative, CRO, email and SMS, and analytics, all working from one plan on one platform, Rallio AI. We are headquartered in San Diego with offices in Irvine, New York, and Orlando plus a remote team.

**What makes the Ignite Visibility team different from other agencies?**
Most agencies bolt software onto services. Ignite Visibility pairs 600+ human experts with Rallio AI, our proprietary AI platform for local growth, so strategy, content, reputation, and attribution run on one centralized brain. The result is one unified ecosystem and higher ROI than a traditional agency. That focus has earned Clutch's #1 SEO Agency in the USA and 4 Search Engine Land Awards.

**How does the team use AI?**
Ignite Visibility believes human expertise should be amplified by AI, never replaced. Our experts run every engagement on Rallio AI, one platform that unifies the Social & Reputation Command Center (social, content, and reviews), the Amplify AI Suite (AI SEO content, video, and microsites), RADIUS Local Leads (local visibility and lead generation), and RevIntel (revenue attribution into paid-media bidding).

**What types of businesses does the team work with?**
Ignite Visibility is engineered for enterprise, franchise, and multi-location growth, managing 50,000 locations for 2,500+ brands, including 400+ multi-location brands. We specialize in the compliance, brand governance, and local-to-national coordination multi-unit brands require, across Franchises, Home Services, Automotive, Healthcare, Legal, Insurance, Financial Services, and eCommerce.

**How much does it cost to work with Ignite Visibility?**
Engagements typically run $2,000 to $10,000+ per month, scaled to your locations and goals, with entry programs starting at $2,000 per month. Ignite Visibility offers flexible contracts with no rigid long-term lock-ins, so the partnership is earned every month. Ask about our Local & Multi-Location, Franchise, and Enterprise SEO packages.
